title: Helmet Headset
tagline: A cheap Bluetooth neckband taken apart and rebuilt as a helmet headset
summary: Music, calls and navigation voice in your helmet for about ₹1,900–3,350 instead of a ₹5,000+ communicator, using a cheap Bluetooth neckband's own parts: its board, battery, both speakers and its mic. Its board and buttons go in a slim pod stuck to the outside of the shell on the left with VHB tape (about 59 × 37 mm and 17 mm proud, with room for most neckbands' parts; a round play/call button and a dedicated volume rocker for gloves, sealed, USB-C at the back); its battery goes in its own slim box on the back of the helmet (41 × 26 × 9 mm, a TPU cover that snaps on), which takes 6 mm off the side pod (or keep it in the pod); the earbuds' own 10 mm speakers go in printed pucks in the liner's ear pockets; its mic goes on a bendable boom held on the helmet's fixed part, so a modular helmet's chin bar flips up over it. No holes in the helmet: the pod sits along the shell's lower edge, so its wires go straight in under the edge trim (the back box's lead comes down a short grooved channel); besides the neckband, only small hardware bits. General purpose: the helmet's curve is a setting, and the neckband's parts are too (a bigger neckband makes the pod grow).
status: Designed and modelled (v1, checked in CAD, not printed or built yet). Designed first for a modular (flip-up) helmet. By default the battery goes in a box on the back of the helmet and the side pod holds the board (up to 50 × 12 mm) and the keys; the battery has room up to 35 × 20 × 6 mm (300 mAh class). Most neckbands fit, not all; enter a bigger neckband's sizes and the parts grow.
see_sub: The pod on the left, behind the chin bar's pivot (the helmet is a plain stand-in); inside, the earbuds' speakers in the ear pockets and the neckband's mic on a boom.

gallery.caption: The pod low on the left of a modular helmet (a white stand-in), along the shell's lower edge behind the chin bar's pivot: 17 mm proud, the battery in a box on the back
The pod: about 59 × 37 mm and 17 mm proud of the shell at its middle; a round play/call button and the volume rocker in a screwed lid, USB-C at the back
Cut through the pod at the volume rocker: one rubber key over 2 switches, its solid middle on a pivot post; the neckband's board below, on the floor
The pod's bottom long side: the 3 cable notches (speakers, mic, battery) right at the shell, facing down
The pod along the shell's lower edge: its cables leave the notches in its bottom side (facing down, away from rain) and go straight in under the edge trim
The back of the helmet: the battery's slim box (41 × 26 × 9 mm), its lead down a short grooved channel to the lower edge; the side pod low on the left
The back box opened: the TPU cover (snaps on, no screws), the battery, the PETG base curved to the shell with the lead's notch
Opened up: the lid, the TPU keypad (also the gasket), the switch board and the neckband's board
Inside (the stand-in cut open): the left earbud's speaker in its puck in the ear pocket, the neckband's mic on a boom held low on the fixed shell, reaching into the chin bar
The parts that go inside: a speaker puck holding the earbud's own 10 mm speaker, the boom mount and the mic cup
The back box's channel turned over: the groove for the battery's lead on its underside, thin flanges for the tape

part_groups.label: The pod (outside, left, along the lower edge)
The battery's back box (outside, on the back)

pod_body.name: Pod body
pod_body.what: Holds the neckband's board, its battery and the switch board. Its underside is curved to the shell and stuck on with VHB tape; the USB-C hole at its back end, 2 cable notches in its bottom long side, right at the shell and facing down, lined up with the cable channel; 4 pillars for M2 heat-set inserts
pod_body.material: PETG or ASA, a light colour if you can. Open side down

pod_lid.name: Pod lid
pod_lid.what: Rolled edges, holes for the play/call button and the volume rocker, a ridge between them; 4 M2 × 6 countersunk screws

rocker_post.name: Rocker pivot post
rocker_post.what: A tiny 3 × 3 mm post glued to the switch board between the volume rocker's 2 switches: the rocker's solid middle rests on it and tips either way

keypad.name: Keypad
keypad.what: One TPU sheet with 2 keys: a round play/call button and a long volume rocker across the pod (raised + on its top end, − on its bottom end); its edge is the seam's gasket, squeezed 0.2 mm by the lid

usb_plug.name: USB-C plug
usb_plug.what: Seals the USB-C socket when you ride; pull it out by its tab (pointing up) to charge

speaker_puck.name: Speaker puck
speaker_puck.what: Holds the earbud's own 10 mm speaker (taken out of its shell) at the middle of the liner's ear pocket, with a small closed space behind it; the back is hollowed. Optional 40 mm helmet speakers fit it too (set the speaker size)

mic_cup.name: Mic cup
mic_cup.what: Holds the neckband's own mic on the end of the boom; a foam windscreen goes over it

boom_mount.name: Boom mount
boom_mount.what: A thin plate that slides between the shell and the liner (or sticks to the shell) low on the left, behind the chin bar; the boom pushes into its socket

headset_assembled.name: Pod, assembled
headset_assembled.what: The pod with its keypad, lid and plug

bb_base.name: Back box: base
bb_base.what: Holds the neckband's battery on the back of the helmet (batt_at = "back"): its underside curved to the shell, on VHB tape; a groove round its walls for the cover's bead; the lead's notch in its bottom side
bb_base.material: PETG / ASA (light colour). Underside down, supports under the curve

bb_cover.name: Back box: cover
bb_cover.what: Snaps over the base (a bead into its groove) and presses its rim: the seal. No screws

bb_channel.name: Back box: lead channel
bb_channel.what: A short strip with one groove: the battery's lead from the box's bottom side down to the shell's lower edge

params.name: batt_at
params.label: Where the battery goes
choices: in its own box on the back of the helmet (a slimmer side pod)
in the side pod, under the board
params.help: On the back, the side pod is about 6 mm thinner.

params.name: shell_rl
params.label: Shell's radius along the pod (front to back)
params.help: Lay a ruler across the spot: radius = L × L / (8 × gap) + gap / 2.

params.name: shell_rw
params.label: Shell's radius across the pod (up and down)

params.name: run_b
params.label: Back box's channel length
params.help: From the back box's bottom edge straight down to the shell's lower edge.

groups.label: Your neckband (the defaults fit most; enter a bigger one's sizes)

params.name: nb_len
params.label: Board length (along the USB-C)
params.help: The defaults (board 50 × 12, battery 35 × 20 × 6, or a long thin one up to 12 × 50) are room for most neckbands, packed with foam. If yours is bigger, enter its sizes: the pod grows. If the USB-C socket sticks out past the board's end by more than 0.5 mm, add the extra here.

params.name: nb_over
params.label: Tallest part on the board (not the USB-C)

params.name: batt_l
params.label: Battery length
params.help: The neckband's own battery (default room: 35 × 20 × 6, or up to about 50 long if 12 wide or less). The board lies on top of it.

params.name: spk_d
params.label: Speaker diameter (the earbud's own driver)
params.help: The earbuds' own drivers: 10 mm on the Rockerz 255 Pro+. Optional 40 mm helmet speakers: 40 × 5.5.
